stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: At the hilltop settlement of Varenka, archaeologists excavating a Bronze Age storehouse found more than two hundred clay jars, many of them still sealed. The thin layer of charred seeds, ash, and broken pottery beneath the storehouse floor ______ that the building burned at least once before it was rebuilt, a finding that helps explain why the jars resting above that layer survived intact.
explanation: Cross out the prepositional phrases "of charred seeds, ash, and broken pottery" and "beneath the storehouse floor." What's left is "The thin layer ______," and "layer" is singular, so it needs the singular verb "suggests." The present tense also matches "helps explain" later in the sentence.

A.why: You matched the verb to the plural list "seeds, ash, and broken pottery," or to "jars," instead of to the real subject, "layer." "Layer" is singular, so "suggest" doesn't agree with it.

C.why: "Are suggesting" is plural. You let the plural nouns inside the prepositional phrase decide the number, but the subject is the singular "layer."

D.why: "Have suggested" is a plural form. It agrees with "seeds" or "pottery" sitting right before the blank, not with the singular subject "layer."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Fossilized leaves preserve more than a plant's shape. The microscopic pores called stomata that dot a leaf's surface let the plant exchange gases with the air, and plants tend to grow fewer of them when carbon dioxide is plentiful. For this reason, the density of stomata on fossil ginkgo leaves from ancient lake deposits ______ researchers a way to estimate how much carbon dioxide the atmosphere held millions of years ago.
explanation: Cross out "of stomata," "on fossil ginkgo leaves," and "from ancient lake deposits." The subject left is "the density," which is singular, so the singular verb "gives" is correct.

B.why: You made the verb agree with "deposits" or "leaves," the plural nouns right before the blank. The thing doing the giving is "density," which is singular.

C.why: "Are giving" is plural. It fits "stomata" or "leaves," but those nouns are inside prepositional phrases. The real subject is the singular "density."

D.why: "Have given" uses the plural helping verb "have." You followed the plural nouns in the prepositional phrases instead of the singular subject "density."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: The bar-tailed godwit, a long-legged shorebird that breeds in Alaska and spends the winter in New Zealand and Australia, ______ the record for the longest nonstop flight of any bird ever tracked. Satellite tags show that some individuals cross the Pacific in about eleven days without once landing to feed or rest.
explanation: Skip the appositive between the commas ("a long-legged shorebird ... New Zealand and Australia"). The subject is "The bar-tailed godwit," which is singular, so it needs the singular verb "holds."

A.why: You matched the verb to "New Zealand and Australia," the pair of nouns at the end of the appositive. The appositive only describes the subject. The subject is the singular "godwit."

B.why: "Are holding" is plural. The "and" that joins "New Zealand and Australia" is inside the appositive, so it doesn't make the subject plural. "Godwit" is singular.

D.why: "Have held" is plural. You let the compound noun just before the blank decide the number instead of the singular subject "godwit."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: The hand-drawn maps in the archive of surveyor Inés Calloway, who charted the river valleys of northern Patagonia during the 1890s, ______ now available to researchers in digitized form. Historians value the sheets because they record settlements, trails, and river crossings that appear on no official map from the period.
explanation: Cross out "in the archive of surveyor Inés Calloway" and the "who" clause. The subject left is "The hand-drawn maps," which is plural, so the correct verb is "are." The word "now" confirms the present tense.

A.why: You matched the verb to "archive" or "Calloway," singular nouns that sit between the subject and the blank. The things that are available are the "maps," which is plural.

B.why: "Was" is singular, and it also breaks with "now." You made the verb agree with the singular "archive" instead of with the plural subject "maps."

C.why: "Has been" is singular. It fits "archive" or "Calloway," but those nouns are inside the interrupting phrase and clause. The subject is the plural "maps."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In a three-year field trial in central Iowa, agronomists planted narrow strips of native prairie grasses between rows of corn and soybeans. According to the team's latest report, every one of the plots bordered by prairie strips ______ lower rates of soil loss than the comparison plots do, and many of the bordered plots also support larger populations of pollinating insects.
explanation: The subject is "every one," and "one" is always singular. Cross out "of the plots" and "bordered by prairie strips" and you're left with "every one ______," which takes the singular verb "has." The present tense matches "do" and "support" in the same sentence.

A.why: You made the verb agree with "plots" or "strips," the plural nouns right before the blank. "Every one of" gives a singular subject, so it needs "has."

C.why: "Are having" is plural. "Every one of the plots" can feel plural, but its grammatical head is "one," which is singular.

D.why: "Were having" is plural, so it doesn't agree with the singular "one." Its past tense also clashes with the present-tense "do" and "support."
